Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to The Indian Hotels Company Limited Earnings 
Conference Call for the Quarter Ended 30th September 2026. On the call, we have with us Mr. 
Puneet Chhatwal Managing Director and CEO, IHCL; and Mr. Ankur Dalwani, EVP and CFO, 
IHCL. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star and then zero on your 
touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded.

Chhatwal. 
Puneet Chhatwal: 
Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining our global conference call for Q2 '26-'27. 
We are pleased to inform you that we have continued our record performance for the 18th 
consecutive quarter, underpinned by our diversified operating model and disciplined execution 
despite macroeconomic headwinds. 
 
Building on this strong foundation, sustained momentum and seasonally strong quarters ahead, 
we are confident of exceeding our previously communicated FY27 consolidated revenue growth 
guidance of 12% to 14% by 300 basis points. Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth 
guidance upwards to 15% to 17%. And within that, the Hotel segment revenue is expected to 
grow by 17% to 19%. 
 
I'll now outline the 10 key highlights of the quarter. Number 1, the strong performance in the 
second quarter. Our consolidated operating revenue grew 22% year-on-year to INR2,484 crores. 
Operating EBITDA grew 24% year-on-year to INR706 crores, yielding operating EBITDA 
margin of 28.4%, an expansion of 50 basis points. 
 
Our bottom line grew by 23% to INR349 crores. Consolidated Hotel segment operating revenue 
and EBITDA grew by 25% and 30%, respectively, driven by the strength of our diversified 
brandscape and unique portfolio. 
 
On the stand-alone basis, we continued to deliver strong performance with operating revenue 
growing 26% year-on-year to INR1,336 crores and operating EBITDA growing by 40% to 
INR520 crores, yielding operating EBITDA margin of 38.9%. That represents an expansion of 
400 basis points. Our stand-alone PAT margin stood at a healthy 27%. 
 
Our performance is not defined by a single year, but by sustained execution over time. Over the 
past 5 years, we have delivered double-digit CAGR across revenue, EBITDA and PAT, 
reflecting consistency and structural strength of our business model. Importantly, our current 
growth rate is ahead of our 5-year CAGR, demonstrating a clear acceleration in our growth 
trajectory. 
 
Moving on to the second highlight is double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands on the back 
of strong domestic demand. The Indian hospitality sector witnessed multiple macro headwinds

during this quarter. Ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia resulted in elevated fuel prices, 
leading to reductions in airline capacity and higher airfares, which moderated travel demand, 
particularly in certain international and long-haul corridors. 
 
Despite these challenges, domestic demand remained resilient, supported by multiple large 
MICE events such as the BRICS Summit. We delivered double-digit RevPAR growth across all 
our brands, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our market 
positioning. 
 
This translated into market share gains with occupancy increasing from 75% in Q2 last year to 
82% this year. Our continued focus on efficient revenue management and operational excellence 
enabled us to achieve 28% growth in stand-alone RevPAR and 25% growth in consolidated 
domestic hotel RevPAR. 
 
Number 3, as a highlight was asset management driving pricing power in key cities. Our asset 
management strategy continues to be a key driver of growth and value creation. During the last 
financial year, we completed major upgrades across several marquee hotels, including Taj 
Palace, New Delhi, President, Mumbai, Taj West End, Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada in Goa and 
Taj Lake Palace, Udaipur. These investments are now translating into stronger pricing power 
and improved operating performance across key markets. We expect this momentum to continue 
through the second half of FY27. 
 
A strong example is Taj Palace, New Delhi, where room revenue grew 132% in Q2 FY27 versus 
last year. In September, the hotel crossed INR100 crores in monthly revenue for the first time 
while delivering a very high CGOP margin. This underscores our ability to deploy capital in a 
disciplined manner, unlock value from our existing assets and generate strong returns with a 
relatively short payback period. 
 
Number 4, portfolio growth. We continue to deliver industry-leading portfolio expansion with 
47 hotels signed and 20 hotels opened in H1 FY27, taking our portfolio to 670 hotels with over 
69,000 keys in operation or under development. With 390 operational hotels, we are on track to 
cross the 400 hotel milestone in November or latest before the end of Q3. Our pace of growth is 
accelerating. It took us 110 years to reach 100 operational hotels in 2013, another 12 years to 
double that to 200 in 2025 and just 18 months to approach 400 operational hotels. 
 
More importantly, our growth remains capital-light and very well diversified. Of the over 34,800 
keys in our pipeline, 94% are capital-light, comprising 81% under management contracts and 
13% under capital-light leases. This model strengthens earnings visibility while limiting capital 
requirements, which, in return, enable us to scale our portfolio, expand our margins and improve 
returns on capital. 
 
This is a very interesting phase because we have given a guidance under Accelerate 2030 of 700 
hotels portfolio. We will revert to all the investors by middle of November with a revised target 
of the 700 because we should get to that number definitely before the end of this financial year.

Number 5, management fee growth backed by new openings momentum. Our asset-light growth 
driven by management contracts continues to translate into strong growth in management fees. 
During the quarter, management fee income grew by 25% to INR156 crores from INR125 crores 
in the corresponding period last year. This growth was driven by 25% increase in managed room 
inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new revenue streams like brand fees from various 
branded residential and villas projects. 
 
This performance despite temporary headwinds, reinforces the resilience of our asset-light 
business model. Looking ahead, we remain confident of sustaining management fee growth at a 
high teens CAGR, supported by a strong pipeline of hotel openings and incremental 
contributions from newly added hotels. 
 
Number 6, select service business consistently driving and delivering on all fronts. IHCL's select 
service business comprising of Ginger, Qmin, Ama and Tree of Life continued to deliver robust 
performance. Consolidated revenue of Ginger stood at INR193 crores, delivering 25% growth 
year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 40%. Our growth brands continued to scale new 
milestones this quarter. 
 
Ginger became India's first hotel brand. Yes, it became India's first hotel brand to reach 100 
operational hotels and is on track to reach 150 by March 31, FY27. Qmin now has over 130 
outlets. Ama Stays & Trails has crossed 400 villas and bungalows and Tree of Life has grown 
to a portfolio of over 50 resorts. 
 
Number 7, a strong balance sheet with healthy cash reserves. Our balance sheet continues to be 
healthy with gross cash reserves of over INR4,350 crores. This provides us with the flexibility 
to continue investing in brand and revenue-enhancing initiatives, including hotel upgrades, 
expansions, greenfield developments and asset management opportunities such as strengthening 
our marquee food and beverage concepts. 
 
Number 8, Oriental Hotels merger as a strategic transaction, unlocking synergies. During the 
quarter, we also announced strategic merger of OHL with IHCL, which will unlock operational 
synergies, expand asset ownership and accelerate long-term revenue growth. It will also leverage 
IHCL's strong balance sheet to fund inventory expansion and product upgrades, further 
strengthening the portfolio's premium positioning. 
 
The all-stock transaction with a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL 
shares is expected to drive 6% to 7% upside in our stand-alone operating revenue in FY28. We 
do not expect this transaction to come into force before 1st April of next year. So the guidance 
that we are providing of 300 basis point increase in the total revenue for the year does not include 
revenues from OHL. That will come on top next year. 
 
The merger will further simplify the group's holding structure by increasing IHCL's direct 
ownership, thereby streamlining governance, optimizing corporate overheads and enhancing 
operational efficiency. The scheme of arrangement has been filed with the stock exchanges. And 
as I already mentioned, the appointed date remains at 1st April 2027.

Number 9, Paathya staying aligned with our ESG++ initiative, Paathya, that is what we call it, 
is well on the journey towards our 2030 targets. It remains absolutely on track, and IHCL now 
uses 41% energy from renewable sources and has installed over 361 EV charging stations across 
170 locations in India. 
 
Continuing our journey of eliminating single-use plastic, IHCL has installed bottling plants at 
92 hotels and achieved 54% recycling of water used in Q1. IHCL currently partners in operating 
83 skilling centers across 20 states in India. Since 2020, we have trained over 56,000 youth or -

Hotel Brand. And we are extremely delighted that this is happening again and again year after 
year, including Taj being recognized as India's strongest brand across all sectors, which was 
announced in the previous quarter.

their 3 Michelin key's rating for the second consecutive year making them the only 2 hotels in 
India to receive this distinction. We are grateful to our loyal patrons and dedicated colleagues 
who have played an integral role in making Taj the epitome of hospitality and luxury. 
 
Finally, looking at the remainder of year, which is H2. As we look ahead, we remain confident 
of delivering on our upgraded guidance of 15% to 17% revenue growth for FY27 with Hotel 
segment growing from 17% to 19% with sustained margins and strong cash generation. We are 
also on track to achieve our target of 50 hotel openings this year. 
 
That means 30 hotels are expected to open in the second half of this year. With strong 
foundations in place, disciplined execution and a clear strategic direction, we remain focused on 
delivering sustainable, profitable growth and long-term value for all our stakeholders.
